doc.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

title: Corky Corcoran: Lunceford, Sonny Dunham, and adoption by Harry and Betty Grable
summary: Corky's story of jamming at 15 for Jimmie Lunceford, joining Sonny Dunham then Harry James, and being adopted so he could stay in the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: a key to the union, I can go down there and anytime and jam anytime I want, why don’t you guys come down and jam with me?” So he keeps bugging the piano player. So 2:00 in the morning, whatever, they go down to the union. He says, “Okay, kid, what do you want to play?” “Well play ‘Cherokee.’” And that was the tune. Okay. “What key do you want to do it in?” “All of them. We’ll start with C and go around the horn.” “Really? What tempo?” “Well about [beats rhythm]” So he gets done playing, “Can you play a ballad?” He plays “Body and Soul.” He calls up Jimmie Lunceford, 3:00 in the morning. Mr. Lunceford. They always referred to him as “Mr. Lunceford,” not Jimmie or boss, but “Mr. Lunceford, this is so-and-so.” “Well it’s 3:00 in the morning, what are you doing?” He says, “I have something, you’ve got to come down and hear this young man play.” “What are you talking about?” “You’ve got to come down and hear this kid play.” So Lunceford gets dressed, Corky says, and he comes down and he’s in his overcoat and he says, “Okay what are you gonna do?” He plays for him and he says, “How old are you?” He said, “I’m 15.” “You play like that, how long you been playing?” “I don’t know two or three years.” “You play like that?” He says, “Yeah.” “Okay give me your phone number.” So a few months passed, he gets a phone call, “Corky this is Mr. Lunceford, I’m calling from Los Angeles.” And Corky says, “Yes.” He says, “My friend Sonny Dunham is starting his band and he’s looking for young talent and I told him about you and I’d like to send for you to come to Los Angeles to audition for him.” And Corky says, “Well you mean I have to stand there and play all alone?” He says, “No, I’m going to feature you with my band at The Palladium.” And he says, “Well I’ll have to go ask my mother.” So they fly Corky’s mother and Corky, and here he’s at The Palladium playing with Jimmie Lunceford. Sonny Dunham hires him. The talk is all over. Big article in DownBeat, 15-year-old saxophone player. You ask anybody that grew up in that era. They said, “Corky Corcoran, are you kidding me?” Everybody said “Wow look at this.” So now he’s playing in New York. And Sonny Dunham says, “Harry James is coming in to see you tonight.” He says, “Harry James, Whoa.” So he says, “Harry walks in there with his entourage and Sonny Dunham calls me up and Corky says, “I played four measures, four measures of a ballad, Harry got up and walked out.” He said, “Well I really impressed him.” So he goes back to his hotel room at 2:00 in the morning and the phones rings, and he says, “As Harry James’ manager we’d like to have you — Mr. James would like to have you join the band.” And Corky says, “Well you know I’ve got another six months to go with Sonny Dunham you know.” And he says, “No, we’ve taken care of that.” So he says, “The bus leaves at 9:00 in front of the Roosevelt Hotel be there.” Click. So now he’s on the band.
That’s sort of like a basketball team. Like you’ve been traded man.

Oh yeah I know. No it’s the same thing. Now Corky’s telling me this and we’re breaking up. So Corky says, so now, in those days you did movies, you know they put the bands in movies. People wouldn’t care about the movie, they’d want to go see the band, right? So we still do music from this, the worst motion picture in the world, Saving — no, not “Saving Private Ryan” no, “Private Buckaroo.” Awful movie. It has the Andrews Sisters, has one of the — has Joe E. Lewis the comedian, and Harry James. And Harry James is a bugler that doesn’t play, and has to be the bugler from — it’s stupid, dumb. Donald O’Connor’s first movie. And Corky is 16 now. So he’s got a role in the movie. So Corky says, “We’re out playing catch out in the sound lot of the movie theater, and this guy comes up to Donald O’Connor and he says, “How old are you?” Donald O’Connor says, “I’m 16 years old” or 17. He says, “Yeah? Where do you live?” And he says, “I live in Los Angeles.” “Where’s your parents?” “My mother is sitting over there.” “Oh. And who are you?” And Corky says, “Who am I? What have you been living under a rock, I’m the famous saxophone player with Harry James.” And he says, and he says, “And where do you live?” He says, “Tacoma, Washington.” “How old are you?” And he says, “I’m 16” or 17. And he says, “And where’s your parents?” “Well if I live in Tacoma where do you think they are?” So this is a truant officer. So he goes over to Harry James and he goes, “You are in violation of the child labor law act of California. You have to send him back or he has to have a legal guardian.” Now it gets better. He goes to Betty Grable, who is also on the set, “Okay Mrs. Corcoran, this is Harry James.” “Well is Corky all right?” “Yes. We have a question to ask you. We would like to adopt Corky.” “What? Okay.” So Harry and Betty Grable adopted Corky Corcoran so he could stay in the band, and he stayed on the band 38 years. So that’s why he was always there. And on every recording I’d say, 90 percent of Harry James recordings there’s always a Corky Corcoran solo. Maybe it could be four bars, eight bars, feature, always. Corky could do no wrong.
